ink.note: Source is hsl(var(--measure-accent)) on a light page and a fixed hsl(210 50% 23%) on a dark page; both resolve to this value.

backdrop-dark-page.note: Replaces backdrop under .dark; shown as the rounded panel.

value.purpose: The number on the navy pill; the largest and only bold type in a picture.

value-unit.purpose: The "mm" after the number, at 75% opacity, 3px after it.

note.purpose: A few words naming a thing on the picture, or a lens caption.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Under the value pill and the lens disc only.

shadows.name: tray-shadow
shadows.purpose: Soft shadow round the foot of the tray.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.purpose: Under anything standing on the floor (0.16 under a tripod, 0.22 under each foot).

shadows.name: wall-foot
shadows.purpose: Shade along the foot of each wall.

shadows.name: edge-fade
shadows.purpose: Fades the room softly into the card at the frame.

motion.name: read-pulse
motion.purpose: The read point; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

camera.mirror: front left, or front right when only the left side has a wall; once per shower shape

framing.readingFocus: reading points + tray top corners + two tray corners at 900mm, grown 200mm
framing.wholeRoomWhen: no particular reading (marking out, laser over a corner)

marksPx.lensWallGap: drawn 18% larger, zoomed until the 50mm spans the radius

themes.dark: room unchanged on a #e6e4e0 panel rounded 14px; measuring ink fixed at hsl(210 50% 23%)

narrative.overview:
Each card is a page from one architect's drawing set: the customer's own shower standing on its tray in the corner of a pale bathroom, seen from one fixed isometric angle, with every edge a fine dark line and every surface a flat plane of white or light grey. Nothing in the room carries colour. Colour belongs only to the act of measuring: the laser's red light, the tape's yellow blade, and the navy of the dimension, the points and the number.

The pictures are calm and dense with information in one place only. The room is drawn once per shower shape and never moves while a number is typed; each card comes in close enough to its own reading to read it, and no closer, and keeps the whole tray in view so the customer knows which side and which end they are on, except a reading at a wall, which comes in close on that end of the glass (Matt, 12 November 2026). Where a reading is too small to see across the room (a 50mm gap, a 10mm line), a magnifying lens shows it close up, with the glass cut away.

The world replaces flat, face-on CAD drawings with grey slabs and dashed lines; it does not go back to them.
keyCharacteristics: One camera for the whole deck: 33° turn, 33° rise, one light over the eye's left shoulder.
Flat planes, fine dark outlines, two room line weights (1.05px and 0.6px).
Three meaning colours only: laser red (light), tape yellow (the tool), measuring navy (what to measure).
A draughtsman's dimension with filled arrows and a large navy number pill is the loudest mark on every card.
Small readings go in a lens whose close-up is a cutaway without glass.
The room stays light on a dark page, on its own light panel.

rules.name: The Three Meanings Rule
rules.body: Red is the laser's light, yellow is the tape, navy is what to measure. Each means one thing on every card, and nothing in the room is drawn in any of them.

rules.name: The Light Is Not An Edge Rule
rules.body: A laser line is always drawn as light: an 8px halo at 16% opacity, a 2.2px red line, and a 0.7px pale core at 85%. Where it runs on past what matters it fades out along its length; a secondary line is drawn at 45% opacity. A beam is never a single hard stroke.

rules.name: The Material Blue Rule
rules.body: The masking tape keeps its real light blue; it is a material, so it may sit in the room. It must never be used for a measuring mark, and navy must never be used on the room.

rules.name: The Number Is The Hero Rule
rules.body: The value pill is the largest type on the picture and the only bold type. Nothing else on a card may be set larger or heavier.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Every face is toned by the same lamp over the eye's left shoulder. Never light a single object from its own direction to make it read.

rules.name: The Contact-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows sit under things that stand on the floor and nowhere else, except the 1.5px lift under the pill and the lens.

dos: **Do** draw every picture in a deck from the one camera (33° turn, 33° rise, mirrored only by the shower's shape) and the one lamp over the eye's left shoulder.
**Do** frame a reading on the reading and the whole tray, grown 200mm, and never closer than 0.27px per mm.
**Do** size every stroke, mark and label in screen pixels: 1.05px outlines, 0.6px fine lines inside objects, 1.5px dimension lines.
**Do** tone faces flat by the light: lit side walls white, the back wall `wall-shade`, cuts through walls `cut`, the tray front `tray-shade`.
**Do** mark every measurement the same way: navy start dot, read ring (red when the laser lights the blade), arrowed dimension, navy number pill on the line or beside it with a leader.
**Do** use a lens only for a reading too small to see across the room, and draw its close-up as a cutaway without glass.
**Do** keep the room light on a dark page, on its own 14px-rounded warm panel, with the marks still navy.
**Do** describe every picture in one sentence for screen readers.
donts: **Don't** draw anything in the room in laser red, tape yellow or measuring navy.
**Don't** draw a laser line as a single hard stroke; it is always light, with a halo and a core.
**Don't** scale the room to the customer's numbers or move it while a number is typed.
**Don't** change the camera, the light or the mirroring from card to card within a deck.
**Don't** add hard or offset shadows; shadows are soft and sit under things standing on the floor.
**Don't** set any type larger or heavier than the value pill.
**Don't** return to face-on CAD drawings with grey slabs and dashed lines.
